description_en: Sundarī Coka ("beautiful courtyard") built by King Siddhinarasiṃha Malla in NS 767 (1647 CE) is one of the three royal palaces of Patan Darbar. The three-storey quadrangle is an outstanding example of seventeenth-century Nepalese architecture. Sundarī Coka's courtyard is particularly attractive, featuring exquisite wood-carved elements such as colonnaded bays, ornamental windows, doors andtoraṇas.A screened gallery overlooks the Tusā Hiti from the top floor with two stone pillars on either side of the steps that lead down to the spout.The principal western façade is symmetrical with the main entrance flanked by a statue of Ganeśa to the left and statues of Narasiṃha and Hanumān to the right. The statues rest on raised pedestals. These three sculptures signify Siddhi, Narasiṃha and Malla, and each forms a component of the name of King Siddhinarasiṃha Malla. On the first floor, a central latticed window is decorated with an image of Sūrya riding on a horse-drawn chariot. This central window is flanked by two smaller lattice windows and two slightly larger lattice windows with a unique eight cornered lattice opening. A triple-bayed window on the second floor features a central opening covered with gilt repoussé. The flanking openings used to be decorated with carved ivory elements. Today, the original ivory carvings are kept in the museum and the windows were restored using a composite material resembling the original ivory. A corner lattice window can be found on the south-west corner on the first floor with a projecting three-bay corner window above.One enters the courtyard from the west through the main door with its richly carved jambs and elaborately embellished lintel ends. Its threshold is made of stone, and the arcaded platform of the entry porch is paved with flagstone.The courtyard has arcaded spaces (phalcā) on three sides. The ground and the first floors are separated by a finely carved timber cornice featuring carvedśivaliṅga.Nepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī(13.275 and 19.3.10-11) mentions that the Hatako Vihāra (today known as Hakha BāhāḥLAL0390) was once located at this very site. Thevihārawas moved to its present location to make place for the Royal Palace. The Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust (KVPT) renovated the palace building between 2006–2017.
description_ne: पाटन दरबारमा रहेका तीनवटा चोक मूल चोक, केशवनारायण चोक र सुन्दरी चोकमध्ये सुन्दरी चोक सबैभन्दा दक्षिणपट्टि रहेको छ र यो चोक सत्रौं शताब्दीको नेपाली काष्ठकलाको अनुपम नमुनाको रूपमा रहेको छ । पश्चिमी मोहडामा चोकको मूल प्रवेशद्वार रहेको छ र प्रवेशद्वारमा पञ्चमुखी गणेश, नरसिंह र हनुमान्‌का मूर्ति रहेका छन् । ती मूर्ति क्रमशः सिद्धि, नरसिंह र मल्ल (राजाको नाम) का प्रतीक हुन् । चोकको चारै पट्टि रहेका भवनका झ्याल, ढोका, स्तम्भ र तोरणहरू कलात्मक ढङ्गले कुँदिएका छन् । चोकमा  ढङ्गा छापिएको छ र चोकको बीचमा रहेको तुसाहिटी ओर्लने सिंढीको दुई छेउमा दुई शिलास्तम्भ उभ्याइएका छन् । स्तम्भको दक्षिणपट्टि ढुङ्गाको खटिया छ ।यो चोक सिद्धिनरसिंह मल्लले नेसं ७६७ (सन् १६४७) मा  बनाएका हुन् । नेपालिकभूपवंशावलीमा (१३.२७५ र १९.३.१०-११) यो सुन्दरी चोक बनाइएको ठाउँमा पहिला हतको विहार (हख विहार LAL0390) रहेको थियो र त्यस विहारलाई अहिले त्य रहेको ठाउँमा सारेर यो चोक बनाइएको थियो । केभिपिटिले यो चोकको सन् २००६ मा सुरु भएको पुनर्निर्माणकार्य भर्खरै २०१६ मा सम्पन्न गरेको छ । पुनर्निर्माणकार्य चल्दै गर्दा सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पमा परी चोकको पूर्वी मोहडाको भवन पूरै भत्केको थियो, निर्माण क्रममा त्यसको फेरि पनि निर्माण गरियो ।

historical_events.event_description: King Siddinarasiṃha Malla built the palace including a hiti with a golden spout and many tantric statues. He also established the statues of Pañcamukhī Gaṇeśa and Narasiṃha.

The Government of Nepal renovated the palace during the reign of King Mahendra and established a police post with a small jail in the building. In 1993, the police was moved to the former municipal building on the south side of the square. Sundarī Coka was closed to the public till 2007.

The metal image of Mahiṣāsuramardinī on the eastern façade was added to replace one that had long been lost. The image of Mahiṣāsuramardinī placed in the spout was also lost, though this one was later found. However, a new image was installed after it went missing, and the original one is now kept in the museum.
